evidence_limits: This is a correctness review of the frozen offline foundation, not M4 acceptance, release approval or runtime readiness.

No Docker, Redis, real acceptance case, image build, network service, commit or publication was run. No repository file was edited. Review files were created only in the authorized correctness-review directory.

The reviewer executed only bounded read-only Python probes. The supplied 160-Python/21-script suites and new Go normal/race roots were not rerun; their current outcomes are not independently attested here.
The 81 canonical invocations are the five-profile Go test design inspected in source (63 finish plus 18 cancellation), not canonical invocations executed by this reviewer.

The Go command facade is not target Redis, real ACL, AOF, TTL-expiration-engine, bootstrap, lifecycle, simultaneous-worker or target timing evidence. Reversed and equal-millisecond traces do not prove real concurrent scheduling.
The new case intentionally remains absent from the 18-case runtime registry. The 90-position executable reader and lifecycle belong to a later gate; their absence is not a defect in this slice.
Security and privilege review, including authorization/ACL adequacy, is delegated to the separate security reviewer and is not approved by this report.

The 105 frozen workspace files and copies were rehashed before and after review. Seven additional Go support files were inspected and hashed at review completion; they are outside the supplied freeze. The reported 372 unrelated files and earlier tree/CI claims were not independently exhaustively validated.

independence_assessment.assessment: Substantive independent Go conformance, not merely producer self-consistency.
independent_checks: Go has literal operation, actor, status, mutation-index and fault inventories independent of Python's sequence specification.

Go derives both run IDs, canonical URL/job identities, group lineage/scopes, policy decisions, source/map digests, crawl-policy descriptor digest, reservation IDs and claim transition IDs from semantic constants and existing Go codecs.
Go derives each 44-key WORK block, 57-key REQUEST and 9-key maintenance wire, checks every binary wire part and RESP size, and independently constructs the 90-key union.
Each Go step executes the embedded authoritative canonical Lua through a command-semantics facade; the facade does not implement claim/start/finish/cancel transitions.
Every nonmutating Go row checks write count plus a deep whole-state snapshot, catching timestamp churn and idempotent-looking writes as well as value changes.

Literal Go invariants supplement the Python full-state oracle for the precise blocked tail, per-run counters, job starts/baselines/ordinals, lease deadlines, tombstone expiry and first-start ownership.
independence_assessment.residual_coupling: The detailed expected rate hashes/history and some initial fixture fields remain Python-produced, with actual canonical Lua state and Go schemas as cross-checks. Those are legitimate differential checks, but not separately literal Go formulas for every field. The read-only boundary probe additionally checked per-scope counters/history and immutable global inventories using independent arithmetic.

recommendations.suggestion: Consider adding a small literal per-scope assertion beside the independent run counters: global next_allowed_ms remains 0; group next_allowed_ms equals the latest actual start; each origin retains only its own history, including zero starts for cancelled A.
recommendations.why: The full Python-oracle comparison already covers these correctly. A few direct Go assertions would also guard against a coordinated producer/canonical regression and make the zero-interval history distinction visible without inspecting the full snapshot.

recommendations.suggestion: Consider retaining the successful delayed-measurement boundary (setup+270000 through setup+300000, exactly 30000 ms), its +1 ms rejection, an overlong prefix, and an omitted error now_ms as compact table-driven regressions.
recommendations.why: The implementation passed these targeted probes. Existing shipped tests emphasize short fixed profiles and reject some malformed shapes; these small additions preserve the distinction between case and measurement bounds and explicit error-null shape.

scope: Six frozen changed files: Python specification/compiler/oracle/tests, Go shared-capacity conformance, and two scenario-inventory additions.
Normative shared-capacity semantics and response/wire contracts; canonical request/maintenance planner excerpts; Go codec and command-facade support.
Bounded adversarial correctness probes only; security/privilege ownership and executable reader/lifecycle are excluded.
summary: No correctness defect or blocker found in the frozen offline-only shared-group-capacity foundation. The exact group denial, full-state nonmutation, cross-run identity separation, release/replay accounting and offline refusal boundaries match the reviewed contract. Two optional offline test-strengthening recommendations do not block this verdict.

validated_invariants.invariant: Two distinct runs/jobs/owners/tokens share one immutable group lineage and policy-group map, with different origins and per-run source digests. Global tuple is 2/0; group/origin tuple is 1/0. Both actors use fence 1 and request ordinal 1.
90 possible keys, 89 fixture-owned positions and 45 materialized setup entries are the combined inventory, not a modified operation layout. REQUEST remains 57 keys and maintenance remains 9 keys.

Blocked claims have exactly [CAPACITY_BLOCKED,now,groupScope,1,1,0]. Global capacity is spare; the contender's reservation and all four origin positions stay absent. Equal tuples produce no tightening or timestamp/inventory churn.

Claims, starts and releases account separately per run/group/job. Starts increment once, baseline remains 0 and ordinal becomes 2. FINISH/cancel releases request capacity, not either job lease or cumulative creation/start history.

The first-start latch is not overwritten. Four durable rate records survive release/maintenance with exact history and inventory scores; global next_allowed_ms stays 0 while group/origin retain their start deadlines.

validated_invariants.evidence: shared_capacity.py:259-278; shared_capacity_specs.py:33-49; test_shared_capacity.py:131-150; canonical terminal:7141-7166; boundary probe
validated_invariants.invariant: CJ2_CANCEL_RESERVATION returns RESERVATION_CANCELLED on both initial and replay paths. Explicit mutation indexes prevent cancellation replay from debiting B. Historical FINISH/START replays are nonmutating and historical START carries io_permission=0.

Wrong-owner CANCEL and wrong-token FINISH substitute only the intended identity scalar while keeping the victim run/job/reservation ID and keys. Canonical immutable mismatch precedes any mutation; cancel-after-start is invalid state.

Pending/started reservations have no physical key expiry. Terminal tombstones expire at terminal time+86400000 while the logical reservation expiry remains claim time+60000. Replays do not renew the lease, extend the tombstone or refund capacity again.

Fixture recompilation and canonical-byte comparison reject forged derived state and bool/int substitutions. Observation fields are exact, success now is an integer in its window, error now is explicit null, prefixes are bounded, and case/measurement/lease time bounds are enforced.
